questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-y\le x\le y\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=6{x}^{2}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=6{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{y}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y[{\int }_{-y}^{y}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y\cdot {[{x}^{3}]}_{x=-y}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y\cdot 2{y}^{3}\text{ }\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{4}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,1\le x\le {e}^{y}\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{xy}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{xy}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{1}{xy}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{x=1}^{x={e}^{y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(9-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3y,\,0\le y\le 1\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=5xy.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=5xy.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot 5xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}5{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3y}5{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}5y{\int }_{0}^{3y}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}5y{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=3y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}5y(9{y}^{3}-0)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}45{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[9{y}^{5}]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{y}^{2}}{x}$ is enclosed between the curve  $x=2-{y}^{2}$ and the line $x=1$ for $-1\le y\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type II plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14194035/assets/6c78767d03e3429551498e651d982d99b6ceb72aa73422c5205bef296c9a1754.png)

So, we have 

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2-{y}^{2},\,-1\le y\le 1\}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{y}^{2}}{x}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{15{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2-{y}^{2}}15{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}[x]_{x=1}^{x=2-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}(2-{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}-15{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[5{y}^{3}-3{y}^{5}]}_{y=-1}^{y=1} \\  & =(5-3)-(-5+3) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the lamina that occupies the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{{y}^{3}},\,0\le y\le 1\}.$ Given that the area of the lamina is $\frac{2}{5}$ square units, find the $y$-coordinate of its centroid.
questions.worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Therefore, the $y$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{{y}^{3}}}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{{y}^{3}}}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y[x]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{{y}^{3}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \sqrt{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{5/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{[\frac{2{y}^{7/2}}{7}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{7} \\  & =\frac{5}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
